item.title: 440 players, three days, one venue - the Nations Championship logistics logjam
item.description: The captains of the 12 teams involved in the Nations Championship line up with the tournament trophy and hemisphere shield [Getty Images] Earlier this year, when planning their Nations Championship finals week, Argentina's staff had a request. Would their hotel in Shepperton allow the team to scorch a patch of the hotel garden for an asado – a traditional Argentine barbecue, in which meat on a low grill is cooked over a bed of hot charcoal? Japan were also making arrangements. The Brave Blossoms had a special rice cooker shipped over to supplement the kitchen facilities at their Kensington base. Such are the countless details that go into an unprecedented logistical juggle. The maths makes the bottleneck clear. The Nations Championship brings together more than 550 players and support staff from the world's top 12 teams for six matches funnelled into three days and just one venue - Twickenham. The new tournament has made new, unprecedented demands on organisers. The first was to find enough accommodation in one corner of London, on a notoriously busy shopping weekend, kicked off by Black Friday sales. A block booking was therefore made back at the start of the year to secure beds in hotels from Brentford, Guildford, Cobham and beyond. Not all those establishments had experience of hosting elite rugby teams. So, chefs and team nutritionists convened to ensure that the hotels were braced with sufficient supplies of eggs, chicken and the rest, to cater for the high-energy, high-protein diets of rugby's best players. The demands continue. While their fellow hotel guests might hit the sights, Nations Championship sides hit the pitch. Individual, private training facilities have had to be sourced for each team, with pitches hired out at local clubs, schools and universities. Teams were given the choice of hotels and training grounds based on their world ranking at the start of the tournament in July, with world number ones South Africa nabbing the Teddington base that usually hosts England's opponents on a regular autumn internationals weekend. The choice is all the more important given the logjam of matches means teams will do their eve-of-match captain's run session at their training ground, rather than, as traditional, at the match venue. To get their players, staff and equipment between hotel, training base and Twickenham itself, organisers have given each team use of four vehicles; a team bus, a people carrier, a van for training kit and a truck for moving scrum machines and other heavy items. Once they finally do arrive, Allianz Stadium, which has hosted Sevens, double-headers and schools finals days in the past, has enough changing rooms to comfortably accommodate four teams at once. The higher-ranked team is given the home dressing room in each fixture. Had England lost to New Zealand last weekend, they would be in the unfamiliar away dressing room. item.title: Fernando Alonso to miss Qatar F1 media day with viral illness
item.description: Motorsport photo Fernando Alonso will be absent from Formula 1's media day ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix as he recovers from a "viral infection". The two-time champion will miss the traditional media obligations at the Lusail International Circuit as he aims to return to fitness for first practice on Friday. A statement from his Aston Martin team explained: "Fernando will miss media day today as he continues to recover from a viral infection contracted towards the end of the Las Vegas GP weekend. "He is recovering well, and is planned to return to the paddock on Friday." Alonso failed to finish the race in Las Vegas due to what he described as a broken engine late on at the Nevada showpiece , with the Honda-powered Aston Martin enduring one of its most difficult weekends of the season, given the power-hungry nature of the Strip street circuit. It meant that the Spaniard was unable to add to his tally of seven points, which has seen Aston Martin take its place ahead of newcomer Cadillac in the constructors' standings. F1 arrives in Qatar after a drawn-out saga over whether it would be safe to race in the Middle East amid tension in the region, triggered by war between the United States/Israel and Iran. Lusail Lusail Both the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix were cancelled at the start of the year, though the former later returned to the schedule, albeit racing at Malaysia's Sepang circuit. With safety guarantees in place - and with Liberty-owned MotoGP having raced at Lusail a few weeks prior - F1 confirmed that the Qatar race and next weekend's season finale in Abu Dhabi would run as scheduled to complete a 23-race calendar. item.title: Part of India's Test squad, star cricketer listed as 'Stan Stan' plays local cricket in New Zealand
item.description: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant took part in a local cricket match in Christchurch on Wednesday, using the opportunity to to keep his eye sharp ahead of the second New Zealand Test starting Friday. Pant, 29, is one of the leading six-hitters in Test cricket history. He has hit 108 sixes in 53 matches, the second-highest tally in the format. Six of those sixes came in the first Test in Wellington last week, where his 128 off 153 balls helped India post a record total of 720/9 in New Zealand. The match ended in a draw. Pant's appearance in a local Last Man Stands match came after he was spotted in central Christchurch. One team, Open House Swingers, were down a player and asked Pant if he would fill in, with the Indian star wasting no time picking up the bat to give them a boost. He turned out for the Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones at Hagley Park. The venue is next to Hagley Oval, where he will represent India in the second Test. Listed as Stan Stan on the scorecard, Pant scored 54 off 21 balls, continuing his run-scoring form in New Zealand. "I saw Rishabh going around on an electric bike," Open House Swingers player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald. "So I went and stopped him, and we start talking and taking a few photos and stuff, and I asked him, do you want to play cricket for us? "He was like, OK, I'll come and play for you guys. Then he came and padded up, went batting, and smashed a few sixes." — RP17Gang (@RP17Gang) India bowling coach Morne Morkel said he "nearly fell off my chair last night when I saw that". New Zealand captain Tom Latham described Pant's performance as "brilliant". "He's obviously a real character of the game is Rishabh, so it's great for him to give his experience back to the LMS teams." Safi told the New Zealand Herald that the opposition players did not recognise Pant, who was wearing a blue tracksuit. He also said Pant had used his cousin's bat during the match. "He was asking me to basically give him a single and stuff. Obviously, I was smashing longer sixes than him, and then he was like, give me a turn, let me show you how to hit it," Safi said. The Open House Swingers won the match by 16 runs. India's second Test against New Zealand begins on Friday at Hagley Oval. 136182903

The veteran defender is approaching the end of his current deal, leaving the door open for a potential Premier League switch this summer. Redknapp backs Blues to pounce on Anfield contract uncertainty Liverpool are still weighing up whether to offer Virgil van Dijk a new contract as his current deal winds down. Should the Reds decide against an extension, former midfielder Jamie Redknapp believes Chelsea must capitalise and keep the Dutchman in the Premier League. Van Dijk has anchored Liverpool's defence for nearly a decade since arriving in 2018, coinciding with the club's return as a major trophy-winning force. While Redknapp hopes the centre-back remains at Anfield, he insists Stamford Bridge should be his next destination if an agreement is not reached. item.description: The Dallas Cowboys will have an opportunity to go on their first winning streak of the season on a short week for their traditional Thanksgiving Day game. After blowing out the Tennessee Titans , they’ll go up against their division rivals, the Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles are having a down season, but just broke their seven-game losing streak with a victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Division games are never easy, and both teams are under .500, so it’s a possible toss-up. It would be difficult for the offense to replicate their game against the Titans , but a good outing from them with some improved defense should get the job done. The Cowboys should be the healthiest they’ve been all year with Jalen Thompson returning from injury. Philadelphia isn’t as lucky with former Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton starting for them though Quinyon Mitchell will play with a hamstring injury. Dallas still has questions about their defense’s ability to stop Milton, let alone Saquon Barkley, and whether their offense can be consistent for the first time all year. If the Cowboys can answer these questions, they could win back-to-back contests for the first time all year and get their record back to .500. Can Dallas keep Joe Milton from looking like an All-Pro? item.title: Why the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys play every Thanksgiving
item.description: Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images Thanksgiving football is a loved tradition in America, and the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys are part of the fabric. The Detroit Lions kick off Thanksgiving by hosting the Chicago Bears. It is a tradition each year that the Lions host the first game of the day – but why? Lions started regular Thanksgiving football The Detroit Lions really invented the concept of Thanksgiving football back in 1934. Their owner at the time George A. Richards believed the holiday date could be a good opportunity for ticket sales. Richards had a radio deal with NBC that also allowed the games to be broadcast nationally. Demand for the event was a huge success. While games had been played on Thanksgiving before, it was the Lions who made it a yearly event, and they have been cemented in the schedule ever since. Over the years the Lions’ record is 38-46-2 on Thanksgiving. However, in their last nine games they are 1-8. Dallas Cowboys seized second Thanksgiving slot By 1966 the Detroit Lions’ annual game was televised and, the NFL decided they wanted a second slot. Dallas Cowboys president Tex Schramm volunteered. At the time there were still concerns about playing on a Thursday, with less time to recover, but Schramm felt the financial attraction and home advantage made it worthwhile. With the exception of two years in the 1970s, the Dallas Cowboys have played on Thanksgiving ever since. The NFL added a third Thanksgiving slot in 2006, rotated the schedule each year. The Cowboys’ overall record on Thanksgiving is 35–22–1. item.title: Exeter are PWR 'contenders' says new boss Bishop
item.description: Exeter won two and lost two of their PWR Cup pool matches earlier this season [Shutterstock] New Exeter head coach Oli Bishop feels his side will be title contenders this season in Premiership Women's Rugby. Bishop was promoted to lead the Chiefs over the summer after Steve Salvin left to become forwards coach with Wales. The former Ealing and Wasps coach has spent 13 years coaching in the top flight and takes over an Exeter side that he helped finish third last season before a late 40-38 loss at eventual champions Saracens in the play-off semi-finals. "The girls are in a good place," he told BBC South West. "We're not changing huge amounts of things, our DNA is our DNA. "We've looked to bring in an extra coach, this is the first time Chiefs have had three full-time coaches and I think that's going to make a huge difference to what we can do and the detail we can go to. "So I would say that we're going to be contenders, but I'm also going to say I think this is probably the most competitive season that we're going to see out there this year." Oli Bishop took over as Exeter head coach over the summer [Shutterstock] Exeter have had to wait an extra week to begin their campaign in the nine-team PWR. They start the season with a tough trip to a Bristol side that ran in eight tries in a 48-21 win at Harlequins last week and have brought players including England star Ellie Kildunne and Wales flanker Bethan Lewis. Exeter have kept most of the squad that got them to the final four in June as they prepare to return to league action after the autumn's WXV matches. "A big thing for us is continuity and cohesion," Bishop added. "We're really happy with the squad and staff that we have and that's why we kept as many as we could at the end of the season. "So we'll be looking to build, we'll be looking to try and do things slightly differently, but again keep our DNA and keep our identity how we want that to be. "Me and Steve worked a lot last year on the culture and identity of this place and how we would change things from the previous way it was being run. "I was 100% on board with that, I've made a couple of tweaks here and there, but they're small changes. "I'm wanting the girls to go out on the weekend and be brave, take the opportunities that are there and be able to express themselves with a clear understanding of how our DNA influences the way that we play."

item.title: Tom Brady confirms what his relationship with Peyton Manning is like now
item.description: Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Roc Nation Tom Brady and Peyton Manning had one of the most historic rivalries not just in the NFL but in all of sports. During their time as players Brady won a record seven Super Bowl championships, while Manning picked up two. However, Manning had the upper hand on the MVP front, securing the award on five occasions compared to three for Brady. Two greats of the sport going head-to-head for over a decade, of course, led to some tension on the field. But it is in their post-careers that they seem to have become much closer. Tom Brady admits he and Peyton Manning are ‘much better friends now’ Speaking on Fox Sports this week, Brady was asked: “Mahomes-Allen really feels like Brady-Manning to me. How did you balance the rivalry with any friendship?” He went on to say he and Manning were not great friends while actively competing in the NFL before admitting they are ‘much better friends’ now. Brady said: “I don’t think Peyton and I had a great friendship until we were both retired. We’ve always enjoyed each other, we’ve always been very friendly, and I want to say we both had so much respect for each other. “There’s nobody that I loved watching play quarterback like Peyton, but we’re much better friends now that we’re not competing on the field against each other.” Manning has been similarly complimentary since the former New England Patriots star decided to call time on his playing career. Speaking back in 2022, Peyton stated that he appreciated his friendship while praising Brady’s dedication, discipline, and commitment. He said: “To do it as long as he did, at the highest of levels is absolutely incredible. It was an honour and a privilege to compete against him on the field, and I truly appreciate his friendship off the field. “I have always admitted and respected his competitiveness, his dedication, his discipline, and his commitment to being the best.” Read more: Fernando Mendoza shares telling insight into Tom Brady’s influence on Raiders Colin Cowherd shares private Aaron Rodgers – Mike McCarthy story that he’s ‘never told’ before Skip Bayless drops ‘impressive’ Rams verdict after win over Packers

item.title: Kentucky Football seeing good ROI on roster spend
item.description: There’s no getting around the fact that Kentucky hasn’t won a football game since Oct. 24, when the Wildcats toppled Vanderbilt 34-17 in Lexington. Three straight losses have derailed whatever College Football Playoff hopes UK may have had. Still, it’s important to take a step back and appreciate everything this team has accomplished so far. With eight regular-season wins and a bowl game still ahead, Will Stein is proving you can win at Kentucky without the hefty resources available to big dogs like Alabama, Georgia, and Texas A&M. The Gator Analytics account on Twitter posted a fascinating graphic of SEC roster-spending ROI that shows just how well Stein has done in Year 1 with the budget he had. Here’s the methodology behind it: Wins are adjusted for strength of schedule. ROI is calculated as schedule-adjusted wins per $10M in estimated roster spending, using The Athletic and NIL-NCAA. Bars show the range based on spending estimates, while dots represent the midpoint of the ROI range.Again, those middle eight teams could be ranked totally differently if you use different sources/ranges so it really is more about looking at the extremes. item.title: ‘Deep shade’ – NFL fans convinced Mike Tomlin took subtle digs at Mike McCarthy on Minecraft stream
item.description: Mark Cornelison/Lexington Herald-Leader/Tribune News Service via Getty Images Amid the chaos unfolding with Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy and the Pittsburgh Steelers, Mike Tomlin’s comments on his latest Minecraft stream have earned some attention. Since being replaced by McCarthy as the Steelers’ head coach, Tomlin has taken on other ventures, pursuing his career as a broadcast analyst while also sharing his world-building on the popular game Minecraft. And on the latest edition of his Minecraft live stream, Tomlin’s comments were perceived by many as slight jabs at his replacement in Pittsburgh. Mike Tomlin’s ‘athletes are taken care of’ comments during Minecraft livestream gets fans talking During his personal livestream, as Mike Tomlin showed off the world he built on Minecraft, he took fans on a virtual tour of the MLS stadium he had constructed in the game. Tomlin discussed the specifics of the design and how it was driven by ensuring player comfort and security, an issue the Steelers have reportedly faced under Mike McCarthy. “Always wanted to represent how athletes are taken care of in the bowels of facilities,” Tomlin said on stream. “Here’s a lounge area. Here’s a locker room area. There’s always cool carpeting and flooring and interior design in these spaces. I kind of wanted to represent that with the colour schemes and so forth. Always in the training area, I’d always have training tables represented, hot tubs, cold tubs, that kind of reflect that space.” Understandably, many fans saw the timing of the stream and his comments as a shot fired by Tomlin at McCarthy. One fan wrote: “I would imagine the Steelers could use this type of detail right about now.” Another fan quipped: “McCarthy would be installing an ice cream machine in his office.” Similarly, a third fan also took a dig at McCarthy’s reported affinity for ice cream: “Sad that Tomlin didn’t include any ice cream sandwiches in the training facilities.” A fourth fan suggested they were enjoying the timing of Tomlin’s stream and comments: “This is some deep shade and I’m here for it.” Similarly, a fifth fan pointed out the interesting timing of Tomlin’s stream: “This dropping on the same day as the Rodgers-McCarthy s*** is so f****** funny!” And lastly, one final fan praised Tomlin’s emphasis on player comfort: “Even in a fantasy world, Mike Tomlin is still out coaching his peers!” While Tomlin may not have intended for his comments to be a dig at his former team and coach Mike McCarthy, the timing of it has led to people jumping to these conclusions. Tomlin has been active in his break from coaching, primarily serving as an analyst for NBC Sports’ coverage of the NFL. However, the chaos unfolding in Pittsburgh has led many to want Tomlin to return to the franchise he served as the coach of for almost 20 years. item.title: Wednesday results boost Arsenal’s Champions League hopes
item.description: Wednesday results boost Arsenal’s Champions League hopes There were a few positive results from an Arsenal perspective in Wednesday night’s Champions League clashes, keeping the Gunners in the top eight. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Though the manner of Arsenal’s draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday was disappointing, there was no real shame in dropping points against the Bundesliga leaders, especially having played well enough to win. The biggest negative of the result was that it left Arsenal open to being caught by multiple teams below them. Had all the remaining results gone against the Gunners on Wednesday, they would have ended the matchday outside of the top eight. Fortunately, there were a few surprises to keep Arsenal in those crucial round-of-16 places. The big one was Bayern Munich’s shock defeat to Lille . Bayern would have leapfrogged Arsenal on goal difference with a win, but despite taking the lead, they ended up slipping to a 2-1 loss. As a result, they remain three points behind the Gunners. Then Sporting and Manchester United played out a 2-2 draw, robbing either team of the chance to gain on Arsenal. Sporting would have crept a point ahead of the Gunners with a win, but Mauricio Pochettino’s team did Mikel Arteta’s a favour. Looking up the table, another surprising result was PSG’s 2-2 draw with AS Roma . PSG remain two points ahead of Arsenal, but their first dropped points has kept the door open for a possible slip-up later. As a reminder, the top-two finishers in the League Phase earn home advantage in the second leg of all of their Champions League knockout games. If Arsenal can catch PSG and steal a top-two spot, they’d be grateful for it later. But they currently sit in seventh, so there’s plenty of work to do. The key thing is remaining in the top eight, and avoiding an extra two-legged play-off tie in February. 16 points has always been enough to make the top-eight in previous seasons, so Arsenal need another five points in their final three games. One win and two draws would do it, with the Gunners to face Real Madrid (H), Real Betis (A), and Sabah (H) in their final three. Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images

item.title: ‘For another second’ – Ryan Clark suggests Mike McCarthy should be fired from Steelers job
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images After listening to Aaron Rodgers’ account of what has been going on with Mike McCarthy, Ryan Clark suggests it might be time for the Steelers to move on from him. Ryan Clark won a Super Bowl as a part of the Pittsburgh Steelers. The legendary safety was known for his tough-tackling ways during his time with the franchise, and has made quite the media career for himself since retiring from the National Football League. So he has some authority when he speaks about the Steelers, to say the least. There is no escaping the latest fiasco unfolding following Aaron Rodgers’ unbelievable interview about head coach Mike McCarthy. And while Rodgers is already out of Pittsburgh, Clark thinks the other half of the beef should also be removed soon. Ryan Clark says Aaron Rodgers’ account being corroborated by others should see Mike McCarthy sacked The Steelers have been known to be one of the most sound and stable franchises in the NFL for decades. One of the most storied organisations in the sport’s history, they have claimed six Super Bowl titles and laid a foundation of success in Pittsburgh. And it is that legacy to which Clark has appealed when suggesting that McCarthy might just need to lose his job considering everything that has come to light. “I don’t know the financial ramifications or the details of Mike McCarthy’s contract, but Aaron Rodgers’ account has been corroborated by others,” Clark wrote on X. “If that’s the case, I don’t know how the Steelers’ brass allows McCarthy to remain the head coach of one of the NFL’s most storied franchises for another second!” The exact financial figures in terms of how much the Steelers are paying McCarthy is unknown, but he signed a 5-year deal with the franchise at the start of this year. Moving on from him is likely to be fairly expensive. With Rodgers already being released, the issues should simmer down. Although if he really has lost the locker room, it will be very difficult for McCarthy to come back from this. The discussions come just months after Bisiwu joined Barcelona’s youth setup as part of the club’s international recruitment strategy. Furthermore, the likes of Rangers and an unidentified French top-flight side are also said to be monitoring the winger’s situation. A move to any of those clubs would understandably be a top opportunity for Bisiwu to experience a more demanding level of senior football, something that he is yet to receive at Barcelona . Bisiwu faces a challenge for first-team opportunities Bisiwu’s progress at Barcelona is complicated by the competition for places in the attacking positions. A loan to a European first division team could provide the winger with a quicker route towards regular football, but at present, Barcelona have not made a any decision. A loan could support Barcelona’s long-term plan For Barcelona, the decision would be about finding the right environment for Bisiwu’s development rather than just moving him out of the squad and getting him minutes. A successful loan could therefore give him exposure to senior competition while allowing the club to continue assessing his progress. item.title: Eli Manning reacts to Aaron Rodgers comments after being benched by the Steelers
item.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/TGL/TGL Golf via Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has been the talk of the NFL world on the back of initially being benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers before he was released late on Wednesday. On the back of his benching, the veteran quarterback appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and had a lot to say about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Eli Manning has since given his take on the situation saying Rodgers is ‘kind of throwing everybody under the bus’. Eli Manning comments on Aaron Rodgers ‘throwing everybody under the bus’ He also made the point that quarterbacks in general have to ‘take the blame’ when things are not going well. Speaking on The Colin Cowherd Podcast, Manning said: “Yeah, I mean, I think that’s kind of part of being the quarterback. When things are going well, you dish off all the credit. You credit the coaches, the receivers, everybody doing well. You give all the credit elsewhere. “When things are going tough, you’ve got to kind of wear it on your shoulders a little bit, and you’ve got to take the blame. That’s just kind of part of the position. “Quarterbacks and head coaches probably get too much credit when things are going well and too much blame when things are going badly, but that just comes with the territory. “Yeah, this is interesting, and I’m just kind of getting caught up on it a little bit. I saw some of the remarks and, yeah, he was not holding back on this one, kind of throwing everybody under the bus a little bit. But, you know, 22 years in the league, he’s had unbelievable success, but he’s leaving with a b*** right now.” It is an unfortunate end to Rodgers’ stint with the Steelers and it will be interesting to see what he does next. Potential landing spots for the former MVP are already being mooted, including a move to the New England Patriots . The Indianapolis Colts are also down a quarterback after releasing Daniel Jones. item.title: Joshua Kimmich calls out club’s handling of Jamal Musiala as ‘not Bayern-like’
item.description: Joshua Kimmich has criticised Bayern Munich over their handling of teammate Jamal Musiala , describing the club’s public conduct towards the midfielder — who suffers from a neurological condition that causes seizures — as "not Bayern-like". The comments follow public criticism from senior figures at Bayern regarding Musiala’s performances and contract. The player experienced two seizures on the pitch during pre-season fixtures, prompting opposition from the international players' union , FIFPRO. A key squad member has now spoken out, warning that the club risks damaging its traditional family values. "What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. "It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either." Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's ongoing struggles were more closely linked to physical injuries over the past two years, including a badly fractured leg at last year's Club World Cup, rather than his medical condition. "It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added. Musiala and Kimmich are both club and national teammates (Getty) Bayern met with Musiala's representatives on Tuesday to clarify the timeline of events, rejecting speculation that the midfielder concealed his health condition prior to signing his recent contract extension. Both the club and Musiala's representatives accept that he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after extending his contract. "This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said. Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the pitch during two pre-season matches, alarming fans and fellow professionals. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany stated at the time that the episodes were triggered by a change in Musiala's medication. He was rested for the start of the campaign and has since missed games due to a muscle injury. Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Wednesday's defeat at Lille, capping a difficult week for Bayern. Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle on Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga and fallen to 15th in the Champions League standings.

item.description: Senne Lammens howler denies Mauricio Pochettino first Manchester United win in 2-2 draw at Sporting Senne Lammens cost Mauricio Pochettino his first win as Manchester United head coach, as a late goalkeeping error handed Sporting CP a 2-2 draw in the Champions League. United led 2-1 in Lisbon with ten minutes left, but Lammens failed to hold a looping Ivan Fresneda cross under pressure from Luis Suárez, and the Sporting striker finished into an empty net in the 80th minute. It capped a chaotic night for the Belgian. He saved Suárez's weak first-half penalty, only to rush off his line and bring down Maxi Araújo moments later. The gap between the save and the foul was just 75 seconds, and Suárez made no mistake from the spot in the 33rd minute. The draw follows a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in Pochettino's opening game. Fernandes brace undone as refereeing decisions frustrate United Bruno Fernandes had turned the game around on his return to the Estádio José Alvalade. The former Sporting man converted a penalty in the 48th minute after Lisandro Martínez was fouled by Eduardo Quaresma, then scored again two minutes later when a soft long-range shot struck a divot and bounced over goalkeeper Kaique. United also had two goals chalked off. Amad Diallo headed in on 40 minutes, but referee Szymon Marciniak had already whistled for a foul by Youri Tielemans, meaning VAR could not intervene. ESPN described the decision as incorrect. Later, Kaique punched a Fernandes corner into his own net, but Marciniak disallowed it for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu after reviewing the pitchside monitor. Tielemans was then sent off for a second booking in stoppage time. It was United's fifth red card of the season in all competitions. After the game, Pochettino took an ironic tone: "I think it's a good welcome for us after seven days, no?" However, the Argentine told manutd.com that he saw positives from his side's performance. He called on United to start believing in themselves and perform with aggression. "I think we need to encourage, and we need to really believe in our play. We need to believe more and more and more. I think we need to give the capacity and the tools to perform. I think, of course, improving things but that is the way we need to show our aggression. "In the second half, we recovered a lot of balls in the opposite half. We were aggressive and I think that is the way we want to play.” Pochettino's next chance at a first win comes on Saturday, when he takes charge at Old Trafford for the first time against Brentford.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup.
